objects: effect matrix F (J SNPs x T wavelet coefficients); F = sum_{r=1..R} F^(r); gamma^(r) ~ Multinom(1,p); f_jt^r ~ g_t^r; wavelet regression model (5)
assumptions: each gamma^(r) has exactly one nonzero entry; the likelihood is the wavelet regression model (5); a separate effect prior g_t^r is allowed for each r
conclusion: At most R rows of F (SNPs) are nonzero by construction, and with R = 1 the fSuSiE model is exactly the single function regression (SFR) model.
scope: Statement about the prior on F in the wavelet domain; says nothing about the fitted posterior. R is a user-set upper bound (tunable setting), not an assumption.
span: Since each binary vector γ^{( r )} = γ_{1}^{( r )} , … , γ_{J}^{( r )} contains exactly one 1, by contruction at most R rows of F contain nonzeros. The fSuSiE model reduces to the SFR model when R = 1.

objects: ELBO F(q_1..q_L; sigma^2, sigma_0^2); variational factors q_l(b_l); expected residuals rbar_l = y - X sum_{l'!=l} bbar_l'; SER(X, rbar_l; sigma^2, sigma_0l^2)
assumptions: SuSiE model (3.1-3.6); variational family factorizes over the L single effects as in (3.7), with no restriction on the form of each q_l; sigma^2 and sigma_0^2 held fixed
conclusion: The ELBO-maximizing update of one factor q_l, holding the others fixed, equals the posterior of a single effect regression fitted to the expected residuals, so each IBSS step is a coordinate ascent step on the ELBO.
scope: Coordinate-wise optimality only; the source calls joint optimization over q_1..q_L hard. Concerns the variational approximation, not the exact SuSiE posterior.
span: Although jointly optimizing F over q1, …, qL is hard, optimizing an individual factor, ql, is straightforward, and in fact reduces to fitting an SER model, as formalized in the following proposition.

objects: population-2 locus effects beta_2; population-1 stage-1 posterior mean betatilde_1 and precision Omega_1; residual precision psi; scalar tau
assumptions: loci are modeled independently; within a locus effects are multivariate Gaussian and y ~ N(X beta, psi I) in precision parameterization; the population-1 posterior used is the one whose (lambda_0, alpha) optimize prediction in population-1 test data
conclusion: The stage-2 prior for population-2 effects is Gaussian, centered at the population-1 posterior mean, with the population-1 posterior precision scaled by tau: beta_2 ~ N(betatilde_1, psi tau Omega_1).
scope: Per locus, two populations, transfer in one direction (population 1 to population 2). tau is a tunable setting that sets how much population 1 contributes.
span: A parameter τ is added to the precision parameter of the Gaussian to control the contribution of population 1 to population 2; thus, the prior is specified as 𝛃_{2} ~ N ( 𝛃 ~_{1} , ψ τ Ω_{1} ).
